newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arab who filmed Israel police brutality arrested.
newsitem.headline: Arab who filmed Israel police brutality arrested.

text.p: Azam Maraka, the Palestinian who made a videotape of Israeli border police beating Arabs that was broadcast worldwide last week, found himself under arrest by Israeli police on Wednesday.
His brother Hussam found himself in hospital in a neck brace.
Israeli police and the Marakas gave different versions of the incident leading to the arrest and hospitalisation.

Hussam Maraka, 34, told Reuters from Mokassad Hospital where he was taken after the arrest, that Israeli police had harassed his brother at his Arab East Jerusalem shop since broadcast of the video showing the police brutality.
"They have been coming to the shop and harassing us for the past week. We have informed the Justice Ministry of that," Hussam said.
"They told people who know my brother, 'Tell Azam Maraka that he's already a martyr'," he later told Israel Television. Palestinians call those who fall in the nationalist cause martyrs.
Hussam said on Wednesday he and Azam, 41, were inside the shop when municipal inspectors began confiscating vegetables from street vendors.

"I went out to see...An inspector pushed and hit me. I said don't push me, I have a bad back. He began hitting me. Why was he hitting me? I hit him back, no problem. Then the border police and police came and everybody jumped on me," Hussam said.
He could not say exactly what transpired between his brother and the police force.
Jerusalem police said they arrested the brothers when they attacked municipal inspectors who were confiscating goods from illegal vendors working near Maraka's shop.
They said Maraka was now in Jerusalem lockup and that Hussam, who they said felt unwell after he was arrested, was taken to hospital. Police spokesman Shmulik Ben-Ruby denied Hussam had been beaten.
"The two attacked two inspectors and after they attacked them we arrested the two," Ben-Ruby told Reuters.
Two municipal inspectors were slightly bruised in the fracas, Israel's Itim news agency said.

The videotape, which was recorded last month by Maraka, an amateur cameraman, and broadcast on Israel's Channel One television last week, showed two policemen lashing out at six Palestinians caught in Jerusalem without work permits.
In the courtyard of an apartment complex, the two policemen kicked some of the Palestinians in the head, kneed another in the stomach and made others lie on the ground and do push-ups.

The Channel One report said the abuse went on for 45 minutes. The video was later broadcast by foreign television stations. An Israeli court charged the two border policemen this week with aggravated assault and abuse of authority.

Israel's attorney-general said on Wednesday before report of the Marakas' arrest that incidents of police brutality against Palestinians like that captured on Maraka's video last month were "widespread".
His remarks contrasted with the reaction by other Israeli officials to the videotape. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had condemned the incident but said it was rare.
